text:
tess: quick poll - should the edge assume HTTP/2 multiplexing by default for upstream streams, or ship with it off until we prove no H-o-L issues?
jamie: Default-on seems nice for perf but i'm nervous: a single long LLM stream could block many short calls on the same conn.
igor: Agree, we need sane knobs. Proposal: multiplexing: auto|off|force, plus tunables: max_streams_per_conn, min_stream_duration_for_dedicated_conn.
chen: If we go auto, what triggers a dedicated conn? duration threshold? token count? we should avoid surprising behavior when clients expect low latency.
sam: Practically, make it route-configurable. For public routes keep auto, internal infra routes can force separate conns for long-running streams.
tess: Good. Second issue: resume and retries. If connection dies midstream, what semantics do we offer? restart the request, or resume partial output?
jamie: Restart-only is simplest. Resume should be explicit opt-in: upstream must implement checkpoints or accept Resume-Token semantics.
igor: If we add resume tokens, they must be authenticated and time-limited. I like stateless HMAC tokens that include route-id, stream-seq, expiry, and a nonce. Edge can mint without DB.
chen: We need to decide who mints: edge or upstream. Edge-minted with HMAC gives control and quota enforcement. Upstream-minted means edge doesn't need signing keys but depends on upstream behavior.
sam: Edge-minted HMAC tokens with single-use nonces would be ideal. Flow: edge issues token at stream start (Resume-Supported: true; Resume-Token: <hmac>) and includes window-ms. If client requests resume, edge validates and resumes if within window and nonce unused.
jamie: Single-use requires state. How do we avoid DB gluttony? Short TTL + in-memory Bloom or LRU per edge instance plus best-effort replay detection might be enough.
igor: Or include a short nonce that is HMAC-derived from stream-id and counter; we can reject replays by keeping only recently-seen counters per tenant in memory. It's bounded.
tess: Also add X-Edge-Retry-Attempt and X-Resume-Attempt headers so upstreams can decide duplication handling.
chen: Telemetry: emit metrics for multiplexed=true/false, resume_requested, resume_success, resume_failure_reason, retry_attempts. Tag with route and tenant.
sam: Example minimal route stanza for the manifest: 
```
route:
  multiplexing: auto
  max_streams_per_conn: 64
  streaming:
    resume:
      enabled: true
      window_ms: 120000
      hmac_key_ref: secret/edge/resume_hmac
      single_use: true
```
jamie: For SLOs we must also record tail-latency impact of multiplexing. Plan: A/B test auto vs off with a mix: 500 short (<=200ms) RPS + 20 long streams (avg 30s) and watch p50/p95 for short requests.
igor: Security note: resume tokens should never expose user data; they must be opaque and MACed. Enforce expiry <= route.window_ms and no longer than 10 minutes by default.
chen: Ops: if resume tokens are single-use and the edge restarts, we risk orphaned tokens. Need a pragmatic GC policy: in-memory seen-set with TTL equal to window_ms, no persistence. Document eventual false-negatives (rare double-resume) and acceptable tradeoff.
tess: Action items: @sam create PR with manifest snippet + impl plan; @igor write token format spec + pseudo code for verification; @jamie run load test A/B and post results; @chen write note comparing edge-vs-upstream token minting and operational cost.
ops-bot: deploy-bot rolled edge-proxy v2.1 to staging. Keep an eye on streaming tests. :rocket:
tess: thanks folks. We'll revisit after jamie's load numbers. If multiplexing shows H-o-L, we'll flip default to off and recommend route-level opt-in.
